text:
maria: Quick heads up — canary eval for onnx-q4k on the new runner shows sampler output order mismatch with baseline. Seeing metric drift (MRR down ~3pts, loss +0.12). I held the canary and flagged the run.

sam: Can you paste the smallest failing diff or logs?

maria: Paste below — the runner logs show seed / order disagreement right after tokenization: 
```
I 2026-03-19T14:05:12.123Z runner: sample_seed=0x7a3f, expected_seed=0x8b2c
I 2026-03-19T14:05:12.124Z runner: sampled_ids: [50256, 27, 183, ...]
I 2026-03-19T14:05:12.125Z baseline: sampled_ids: [50256, 27, 183, ...] (same for first batch)
I 2026-03-19T14:05:12.126Z runner: later batch order differs — batch 3 order != baseline
```
Notably the sample contents sometimes match but the ordering across batched requests diverges (prefix caching + shuffle?).

kevin: That sounds like the deterministic sampler flag we tweaked in PR #4321 (merged yesterday). The change turned on per-shard shuffling by default to spread load: https://git.redwood/4321

tara: If that is the change, impact on quality makes sense — order/seed changes break our eval harness assumptions (we rely on deterministic prefix+batching to compute stable metrics). How big is the canary delta?

maria: Canary numbers (single-run, 20k examples): baseline MRR 0.423 -> canary 0.391; avg NLL baseline 2.13 -> canary 2.25. Std errors small. I also saw sporadic metric flips between runs.

eval-bot: CI: eval-harness-canary (onnx-q4k) FAILED — regression_threshold_exceeded in mrr (job id c-20260319-87)

sam: Ok — sounds triage path: 1) reproduce locally with latest runner tip; 2) quick bisect around PR #4321 (or try toggling deterministic_sampler=false->true); 3) if repro, rollback candidate. Who can run a targeted rerun?

kevin: I can toggle the config and run a short 2k-sample eval against the canary cluster (will use same seed file). Setting `deterministic_sampler: true` should restore old semantics. Trying now.

maria: Thanks. Running a local 2k run with deterministic_sampler:true also — attaching diff of metrics shortly.

kevin: Quick update — with deterministic_sampler:true the short-run MRR returns to 0.421, NLL 2.14. With the merged behavior it's 0.392. So change is the likely culprit.

sam: Good reproduction. That means we should hold the release of runner change. Can we hotfix config on canary and then schedule a rollback PR for the code change?

kevin: I'll push a hotfix toggling the default to deterministic_sampler:true in the canary config and open a rollback PR that reverts the shuffling default and adds an explicit opt-in. PR #4335 created.

tara: Action items: kevin to hotfix canary + open rollback PR, sam to coordinate a quick postmortem note and evaluation checklist, maria to run full 20k canary once hotfix applied and confirm metrics. If hotfix fixes, we keep runner change blocked until we add a harness-compatible test.

maria: Applied hotfix on canary — rerunning full 20k now. Will post numbers in ~40m.

eval-bot: Deploy-bot: canary config update deployed to cluster canary-onnx-q4k (deploy id d-20260319-91) :white_check_mark:

maria: Full run finished. MRR 0.422 (within noise of baseline), NLL 2.13. Regression gone.

sam: Ok decision: hold the merged behavior, merge rollback PR after review, add an eval-harness integration test that runs short-seed-sanity on runner merges to detect sampler/order changes, and add a config doc note about deterministic_sampler.

kevin: Filed follow-ups: 1) PR #4336 — add harness seed-sanity test in CI (short), 2) PR #4335 — rollback + opt-in doc.

tara: Thanks everyone. Looks like a quick rollback will unblock other work. Please add the postmortem stub to the incidents channel and tag me. :eyes:

maria: Adding postmortem draft now. Assigning owners in the doc. :shipit:

sam: Nice catch, thanks for the quick bisect.

kevin: marking this thread resolved once rollback merges. :white_check_mark:
